newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns Boeing against dominating European market.
newsitem.headline: EU warns Boeing against dominating European market.

text.p: The European Commission unexpectedly put Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. on notice Wednesday that their planned merger posed a potential threat to fair competition in the European Union.
"It seems to us that it may raise raise questions regarding a dominant position (in the EU)," European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told a news conference.
Van Miert warned that the Commission would have to examine the deal with a "fine-tooth comb" to assess whether it would strengthen the merged companies' position on any product or geographic markets.
But he declined to elaborate, saying he first wanted to see the details of the deal, which he said was "complex and problematic."

Van Miert, the EU's competition chief, left no doubt that the deal could ultimately be blocked by Europe if it was found to pose serious concerns about competition and if the companies refused to provide remedies.
He said it was quite clear that the deal fell within the EU's purview based on a series of financial thresholds.
The Commission can block foreign mergers if the companies involved do significant business in the 15-nation bloc.
Last year it imposed stiff conditions on the merger of U.S. companies Kimberly Clark and Scott Paper.
The two aerospace companies announced a $13.3 billion stock-for-stock merger on Sunday.
